messages:
maria: heads-up — bringing cicada-lite v1.2 int6 into embed staging. quick sanity: english recall@1/5/10 fine, but spanish queries cluster into two tight islands and recall@1 drops ~8pt. anyone seen language-specific centroid collapse before?

julian: hmm, can you paste the eval digest and what dataset you used?

maria: using multilingual-holdout-v3 (en/es/fr), 50k corpus, queries sampled stratified by lang. eval snippet:```
model: cicada-lite-int6
quant: per-channel int6
batch: 64
metrics: {"recall@1": {"en": 0.78, "es": 0.70, "fr": 0.77}, "recall@5": {"en": 0.91, "es": 0.89, "fr": 0.90}}
cluster_stats: {"es": {"num_clusters": 2, "largest_cluster_frac": 0.62}}
```

sara: whoa largest_cluster_frac 0.62 is suspicious for es. is that in embedding space or after PCA/UMAP?

maria: raw embedding space (L2 normalized). I tried PCA(50) + hdbscan for quick look — same split. UMAP makes it obvious. attaching tiny ascii export:```
es_cluster_counts: [620, 210, 80, 45, 35]
mean_pairwise_cosine_es: 0.88
mean_pairwise_cosine_en: 0.74
```

julian: mean_pairwise_cosine_es 0.88 -> embeddings are too tight for spanish. could be tokenization quirk or subword merge due to vocab tie in int6 kernels. did you compare fp16 baseline?

maria: yes fp16 baseline: recall@1 es 0.78, mean_pairwise_cosine_es 0.71. so quant shift.

sara: try per-channel vs per-tensor int6? also try clamp/scale sanity: sometimes outliers get compressed. can you run a quick compare with symmetric vs asymmetric quant?

maria: running now. command:```
./eval_onboard.sh --model cicada-lite --quant int6 --quant-mode per-tensor --dataset multilingual-holdout-v3 --out /tmp/cicada_int6_pt.json
```

ops-bot: deploy-checklist: staging deploy queued (job id kj-8843) — will run on 8 GPUs, ETA ~10m

maria: results incoming: per-tensor int6 bumped es recall@1 to 0.75 (was 0.70), largest_cluster_frac 0.48. asym vs sym: asym performed slightly better.

julian: ok so quant scheme matters. next check: kernel selection difference between A100 and H100 runtimes? sometimes small ops differ. can you rerun subset on both hardware and compare dotprod distributions?

maria: yes queued small-run on A100 pool. also looking at tokenization distribution:
```
most_common_subword_es: ["que", "de", "el", "la", "\\u00f1a"]
avg_token_len_es: 4.0
avg_token_len_en: 3.1
```
seems spanish tokens slightly longer -> maybe more context per token makes quant brittle.

sara: interesting. also check embedding norm distrib: if int6 compresses norm range, lngs with longer tokens might get pulled toward high-cosine region. try L2-rescale post-quant as a quick mitigation and re-eval recall@1.

maria: tried L2-rescale factor 1.08 (per-lang tuned) — es recall@1 up to 0.77, cluster_frac 0.37. will prepare notebook for ops to add per-lang rescale hook as a temporary.

julian: add to PR: `quant_profiles.md` note and a small unit test using multilingual-holdout. also add an automated smoke that checks max_cluster_frac < 0.5 for any language.

sara: +1. also capture a few failed examples (query + nearest) so product can sanity-check semantics.

maria: capturing examples now and will paste batch of 10 in #eng-ml later.

ops-bot: job kj-8843 finished. logs: `all tests passed`, artifacts: /artifacts/kj-8843/cicada_int6_per_tensor.json

julian: thanks. follow-ups: 1) generate per-hardware dotprod delta plot 2) add per-lang rescale as opt-in in staging 3) run longer recall@10 sweep (100k) before canary.

maria: noted. filing ticket: https://redwood.internal/t/ML-1532 — will assign and add links to eval artifacts. :thumbsup:
